evidence.field: summary, source, permission, licensing, file history
evidence.text: The exact file page identifies 能-seal.svg as a digital vector depicting 能 in Shuowen seal-script style. It links the image to Sinica record 27.80FD and Hanziyuan record S07257, and states that the Sinica picture is CC0 1.0. Commons also marks this vector file CC0 1.0 and records Richard Sears permission material. This is a modern digital drawing of a seal-script form, not a photograph of an ancient artifact or evidence that settles the disputed Shang identification.
evidence.kind: file-level image identity, provenance, and reuse evidence
evidence.title: File:能-seal.svg

evidence.text: The character page labels the displayed form 小篆 and associates it with 說文‧能部. The image is identified as 27.80FD. This supports using the record as a seal-script comparison; the page does not date the displayed drawing to an ancient artifact.
evidence.title: 小學堂字形

evidence.source: CASE 報科學, National Taiwan University Center for Science Education
evidence.field: paleographic analysis, article text and figure captions
evidence.text: The author identifies damaged Shang forms as bear-like 能, but says the few oracle-bone occurrences are damaged and their use cannot be determined. The account describes the Western Zhou bronze form as changing the head toward 㠯, simplifying the body to 月 (肉), and placing the feet side by side. The author presents this as a graphic interpretation; the Shang identification is disputed.
evidence.title: 獼猴與黑熊：甲骨文的「夒」、「猱」與「能」

evidence.source: 劉雲, Fudan University Center for Unearthed Documents and Ancient Chinese Characters
evidence.field: paleographic argument, article abstract and discussion
evidence.text: The author argues that a disputed Shang animal-shaped graph is 鷧 rather than 能, and says securely identifiable 能 first appears in Western Zhou bronze inscriptions. This conflicts with the NTU account that identifies damaged Shang forms as 能. The inspected text does not establish a precise dated first inscription.
evidence.title: 劉雲：釋“鷧”及相關諸字

evidence.source: 許慎《說文解字》, text hosted by Wikisource
evidence.field: 卷十, 能部; entry for 能
evidence.text: The Han dictionary defines 能 as a kind of bear with feet like a deer, analyzes it as 从肉㠯聲, and associates the animal’s firmness and strength with 賢能 and 能傑. This records the Han lexicographic analysis; it does not independently prove that 㠯 originated as a phonetic component rather than reflecting a transformed bear head.
evidence.title: 說文解字/10

search_audit.outcome: Opened the exact 能-seal.svg Commons description page and confirmed its file identity, linked sources, and licensing statements. The Radical 380 file page was inaccessible. Opened the Fudan article for the competing Shang identification.

search_audit.query: 能 Western Zhou bronze inscription paleography bear Shang forms Shuowen
search_audit.outcome: Inspected the NTU paleographic account and the Shuowen entry. The NTU article identifies damaged Shang forms as 能 but says their use is unclear; the Shuowen text gives the Han-era bear definition and graphic analysis.

search_audit.query: 能-seal.svg original file Wikimedia Commons 能 Shuowen seal 27.80FD; 能 字 甲骨文 西周 金文 劉雲 鷧 熊 能 釋讀; 能 说文 小篆 字形 小學堂 27.80FD
search_audit.outcome: Search returned the exact Commons file page and Xiaoxuetang record. Inspected the Xiaoxuetang search result label 小篆 / 說文‧能部 and the official Commons source page. The direct Sinica record open returned a cache miss, so its cited record label and Commons-linked provenance provide the usable verification. The direct Wikimedia SVG original endpoint also returned an internal access error.

gaps: The Shang identification remains disputed: the NTU account identifies damaged Shang forms as 能, while Liu Yun argues the disputed graph is 鷧 and places secure 能 examples in Western Zhou bronze. The damaged Shang examples do not establish their use.
No precise dated first Western Zhou inscription was verified in the inspected sources.

The Commons SVG original-file link was visible on the exact file description page but its direct endpoint could not be opened by the browser. The separate Radical 380 file page was inaccessible and that candidate is not selected.

The selected seal-script drawing illustrates a later script tradition; it cannot independently establish the shape or use of the disputed Shang forms, nor prove a semantic link between the bear and ability senses.

items.period: Seal-script style associated with the Shuowen tradition; the vector file was uploaded in 2011 and is not an ancient artifact image.
items.caption: A modern vector rendering of 能 in Shuowen seal-script style. It shows a later written form and does not resolve whether damaged Shang graphs are 能.
items.alt: Black seal-script strokes forming 能 on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: The exact Commons page identifies this as 能 in Shuowen seal-script style and links it to Xiaoxuetang record 27.80FD. It gives a useful later-form comparison while leaving the disputed Shang identification open.
items.rights: The Commons file page states CC0 1.0 for this vector file and records permission/provenance notes. It links the underlying Sinica glyph picture to the Sinica query-interface CC0 notice. Reuse applies to this asset and specific query glyph, not to bulk database content.

limitations.text: This is a modern vector redrawing, not a photograph or facsimile of a dated artifact. Its later seal-script classification cannot settle the disputed identification or use of damaged Shang forms.
